title: DC-area forecast: Muggy with a hit-or-miss evening shower or storm. Nicer into midweek.
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: A few hit-or-miss showers and storms are possible through about 9 p.m. Otherwise muggy 80s and 70s this evening, down to the low to mid-70s overnight.

What’s next? Drying out and trending a bit less humid Tuesday and Wednesday, with highs in the mid- to upper 80s. More humid Thursday through Saturday, with late-day storm chances returning.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: A few evening hit-or-miss showers and storms are possible, with the chance of a shower or storm lingering latest south and southeast of DC. Otherwise, skies are partly cloudy as humidity slowly decreases. Lows fall to the mid-60s to near 70. Confidence: High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Tuesday): Mostly sunny skies and most likely rain-free. It's moderately humid but eventually less muggy than recent days (dew points dropping to the mid-60s by afternoon). Highs rise to the mid- to upper 80s, with light winds from the north. Confidence: High

Tomorrow night: Mostly clear and pleasant, with lows ranging through the 60s. Confidence: High

📬 Get our forecast in your inbox

Our morning forecast email is back! It's included with every level of support — from Free to Sustainer — delivered 7 days a week. Sign up at: capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

Wednesday is a second straight dry day. It's mostly sunny with highs from the upper 80s to near 90. Humidity remains moderate during the day but begins to increase at night, with lows in the upper 60s and low 70s. Confidence: Medium-High

High humidity (dew points near 70) is back Thursday through Saturday, which also means late-day storm chances return. Highs each day are in the 80s, with overnight lows near 70. Confidence: Medium-High

Sunday is partly sunny, with somewhat lower humidity and lower storm chances. Highs range from 80 to 85. Confidence: L0w-Medium

Today’s daily digit — 4/10: It's still very humid, and a few storms could pop up. But some nicer summer days are oh so close. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for August 17

Blistering heat in 1988 and 1997 sent temperatures into the triple digits—peaking at 105—before explosive thunderstorms brought damaging winds, heavy rain, and rapid cooling.
